correctness.rationale: Utility-based JR tested on each voter's peak requires utility at least 1. Endpoint peaks are mandatory; a run of r omitted interior peaks forces r+1 different bridges, disjoint across runs, exceeding the seat budget. The all-peak committee satisfies JR because every demanded single-candidate utility is at most 1. For odd size the uniform bridge weights rho/(2v) and endpoint peaks rho/2 give budget k and every utility rho. For even size the alternating 1,z bridges (z=h/(h-1+2v)) and endpoint peaks vz do the same, including k=2. All weights satisfy the caps. For a coalition block of size s, alternating normalized voter weights give a bound aB in odd size and a[B+2v-1] in even size, B the incident mass; the one excess even edge has weight at most 1. In either case attaining more than rho_s requires B>s. The incident candidate sets of disconnected blocks are disjoint, so the sum of their B cannot exceed |S|. Both parity expressions equal 2v minus v(2v-1) divided by a denominator that increases strictly with size (also from s=1), hence a utility strictly above rho_k violates the budget. This proves sharpness over all coalitions and the inclusive threshold under strict blocking. The rational and LP checks in the source are finite corroboration, not used as proof or rerun.
